unit.title: Fractions as Parts of a Whole

lesson.title: Review Day: Fractions as Parts of a Whole
lesson.subject: math

contentBlocks.text: This week you explored fractions four different ways. Let's review it all!

Quick review: a fraction is equal parts of a whole, numerator over denominator (Day 1). Fractions can be placed on a number line between 0 and 1 (Day 2). With the same denominator, a bigger numerator means a bigger fraction (Day 3). Equivalent fractions look different but name the same amount (Day 4). Draw a rectangle showing 3/4, then explain whether 3/4 is bigger or smaller than 2/4.
Great work this week — you learned to draw, place, compare, and find equivalent fractions! Next week we'll build on these skills with something new.

objectives: Review fraction basics, number-line placement, comparison, and equivalence
Draw a fraction and correctly compare it to another same-denominator fraction
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Do the quick walk-through review of all 4 days together, out loud.
2. Have the child draw 3/4 and compare it to 2/4.
3. Complete the review worksheet.
4. Celebrate finishing a full week of real fractions work!
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just the skill the child found hardest this week (often equivalent fractions) rather than requiring all four equally
Ready for more: ask the child to find an equivalent fraction for 3/4 and explain how they know it's equivalent
This is a good checkpoint to note which of the week's four fraction skills needs the most reinforcement going forward
teacherGuide.answerKey: 3/4 is bigger than 2/4, since 3 equal parts is more than 2 equal parts of the same whole.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Consolidates this week's Common Core Grade 3 fraction standards (3.NF.1/3.NF.2/3.NF.3) before the course continues, matching the established Day-5-review pacing used across every unit this session.
